stem: Best guess: a physician invests in a restaurant partnership but never works there. Her share of the loss is $20,000, and she has no other passive income. How much can she deduct this year?

choices.explanation: That allowance applies to rental real estate.
Correct. Without material participation the loss is passive and can offset only passive income.

explanation: Without material participation the loss is passive and can offset only passive income.

stem: Single taxpayer, MAGI $140,000, actively participates in a rental with a $15,000 loss, no passive income. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance isn't fully phased out until $150,000.

stem: A cabin is rented 10 days during the year and used personally the rest of the time. What is the tax treatment of the $4,000 rent?

choices.explanation: Correct. §280A(g): rented fewer than 15 days → rent excluded.

explanation: §280A(g): rented fewer than 15 days → rent excluded.

stem: In what order are the loss limitations applied?

choices.text: Passive, at-risk, basis, excess business loss
Excess business loss, then passive, at-risk, basis
At-risk, basis, passive, excess business loss
Basis, at-risk, passive, excess business loss

explanation: Basis → at-risk → passive → §461(l).

stem: A partner's basis is $40,000, including $30,000 share of nonrecourse debt (not qualified real estate financing). Her share of the loss is $25,000, and she materially participates. How much is deductible?
explanation: Basis allows $25,000, but at-risk excludes nonrecourse debt: $10,000 allowed; $15,000 suspended under §465.

stem: Which person qualifies as a real estate professional?

choices.text: An accountant who works 2,000 hours at her firm and 800 hours managing her rentals
choices.explanation: Real estate must be more than half of personal services.

choices.text: An investor who owns 20 rental properties managed by an agent
A full-time property manager who works 1,800 hours in real property businesses
choices.explanation: Correct. More than 750 hours and more than 50% of personal services in real property trades or businesses.

choices.text: A retiree who works 500 hours on his rentals

explanation: More than 750 hours and more than 50% of personal services in real property trades or businesses.

stem: A taxpayer sells his entire interest in a passive activity to an unrelated buyer for a $5,000 gain. Suspended losses are $18,000. He has no other passive activities. What is the result?

choices.explanation: A full disposition frees all suspended losses.

choices.text: Losses stay suspended until other passive income
choices.explanation: A full taxable disposition releases them.

choices.text: All $18,000 of suspended losses is deductible
choices.explanation: Correct. §469(g): a fully taxable disposition to an unrelated party frees the suspended losses.

explanation: §469(g): a fully taxable disposition to an unrelated party frees the suspended losses.

stem: The 2025 excess business loss threshold for joint filers is $626,000. Married filing jointly, 2025 business losses of $900,000 and nonbusiness income of $1,000,000. How much business loss is disallowed under §461(l)?
explanation: Excess business loss = 900,000 − 626,000 = 274,000, carried forward as an NOL.

stem: A vacation home is rented 100 days and used personally 12 days. How is it classified?

choices.text: Rental property; losses subject to passive rules
choices.explanation: Correct. 12 days is not more than the greater of 14 days or 10 days (10% of 100).

explanation: 12 days is not more than the greater of 14 days or 10 days (10% of 100).

stem: Which amount is **not** included in a taxpayer's at-risk amount?

choices.text: Recourse debt for which the taxpayer is personally liable
choices.explanation: Personal liability makes it at risk.

choices.text: Nonrecourse loan from the seller of equipment
choices.explanation: Correct. Nonrecourse debt is generally excluded, except qualified nonrecourse real estate financing.

choices.text: Qualified nonrecourse financing on real estate from a commercial lender

explanation: Nonrecourse debt is generally excluded, except qualified nonrecourse real estate financing.

stem: A married couple with MAGI of $170,000 actively participates in a rental with a $10,000 loss and has $4,000 of passive income from a limited partnership. How much of the rental loss is deductible?

choices.explanation: The allowance is fully phased out.
Correct. Passive losses offset passive income.

explanation: No $25,000 allowance above $150,000 MAGI; the loss offsets only the $4,000 of passive income; $6,000 is suspended.

stem: Which activity is treated as passive regardless of participation (for a taxpayer who isn't a real estate professional)?

choices.text: A consulting business the taxpayer runs full time

choices.explanation: Correct. Rental activities are generally passive per se.

choices.text: A working interest in an oil well held directly
choices.explanation: Working interests are excluded from passive treatment.

explanation: Rental activities are generally passive per se.

stem: A home is rented 60 days for $9,000 and used personally 40 days. Allocated rental expenses: interest and taxes $4,000; operating $3,000; depreciation $5,000. What is the rental deduction for depreciation?

choices.explanation: Deductions are limited to rental income.

explanation: Personal use of 40 days is more than 14 days → residence; the order is interest/taxes, operating, depreciation.

stem: A taxpayer with MAGI of $130,000 actively participates in a rental with an $18,000 loss and has no passive income. How much is deductible?
explanation: The $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% of MAGI over $100,000: $25,000 − $15,000 = $10,000.

stem: A taxpayer works 520 hours a year in a business he co-owns. How are its losses treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. More than 500 hours is material participation.

choices.text: As passive unless he has 750 hours
choices.explanation: 750 hours is for real estate professionals.

explanation: Participation of more than 500 hours in the year is material participation, so the activity isn't passive.

stem: A taxpayer rents a beach condo to guests whose average stay is 5 days. How is it treated under the passive rules?

choices.explanation: Correct. Average use of 7 days or less isn't a rental activity.

explanation: An activity with average customer use of 7 days or less isn't a rental activity; it's passive only if the taxpayer doesn't materially participate.

stem: A high-income taxpayer has a $20,000 passive loss and $15,000 of passive income from a limited partnership. What is the result?

choices.explanation: Correct. Passive losses offset passive income.

explanation: Passive losses are deductible against passive income; the excess is suspended and carried forward.

stem: For 2025, the excess business loss threshold for a single filer is $313,000. A single filer has a $500,000 business loss and large other income. What happens?

choices.explanation: Correct. The excess loss carries forward.
It carries forward as an NOL.

explanation: §461(l): business losses over the threshold are disallowed and carried forward as an NOL.

stem: A taxpayer has $5,000 of passive activity credits but no tax on passive income. What happens?

choices.explanation: Correct. They offset only tax on passive income.

explanation: Passive activity credits can offset only the tax attributable to passive income; unused credits carry forward.

stem: A taxpayer sells his passive rental to his brother at a loss. What happens to the suspended losses?

choices.explanation: Correct. A related-party sale doesn't free them.

explanation: Suspended losses are freed only on a fully taxable disposition to an unrelated party.

stem: A taxpayer works 120 hours in an activity, more than anyone else. Does she materially participate?

choices.explanation: Correct. Over 100 hours and not less than anyone else.
That isn't what the rule says.

explanation: One material participation test is more than 100 hours and not less than any other individual.

stem: An owner rents a building to a C corporation in which he materially participates. How is the net rental income treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. The self-rental rule recharacterizes it.

explanation: Net income from renting property to a business in which the taxpayer materially participates is nonpassive.

stem: A taxpayer dies with $40,000 of suspended passive losses. His heirs get a $25,000 basis step-up on the activity. How much loss is deductible on the final return?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses above the step-up are deductible.

explanation: At death, suspended losses are deductible only to the extent they exceed the basis step-up.
